_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Kiribati covering Micronesian settlement (~2000 BCE), Austronesian seafaring, European contact (Spanish/British 16th-18th century), Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony (British 1892-1979), WWII (Battle of Tarawa 1943, bloodiest US Marine landing), phosphate mining (Banaba/Ocean Island devastation), independence 1979, nuclear testing (Christmas Island/Kiritimati British H-bomb tests 1957-62), climate change existential threat (lowest-lying nation, 2m average elevation, relocation planning).

religion.note: Catholic (Sacred Heart missionaries from 1888, dominant on many atolls); Protestant (Kiribati Uniting Church, London Missionary Society legacy); Baha'i (significant for small population); Latter-day Saints growing; pre-Christian beliefs (Nareau creator deity, anti spirits) largely supplanted but cultural elements remain; church central to community life

ethnic_groups.name: I-Kiribati (Gilbertese)
ethnic_groups.notes: Micronesian; Austronesian language (Gilbertese/Taetae ni Kiribati); extremely homogeneous; te maneaba (meeting house, community centre, political/social hub); seafaring culture; copra/fishing economy; communal land tenure; extended family obligations; outrigger canoe tradition; 'Kiribati' pronounced 'Kiribas' (ti=s in Gilbertese)

ethnic_groups.name: Tuvaluan
ethnic_groups.notes: Polynesian; historically in southern Gilbert Islands; separate country since 1978 (Tuvalu split from Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony)

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Banaban (indigenous to Banaba/Ocean Island, ~5k, phosphate mining devastated homeland, British Phosphate Commission mined 1900-79, most relocated to Rabi Island Fiji, sovereignty claims); Chinese (small business community); European (few)

country_profile.time_zone: GILT (UTC+12, UTC+13, UTC+14); Line Islands (UTC+14, first place on Earth to see new day)

independence.from: United Kingdom (Gilbert Islands; Ellice Islands separated 1978 as Tuvalu)

country_profile.notes_unique: Most climate-vulnerable nation (average elevation 2m above sea level, highest point 3m (Banaba excepted), existential threat, some atolls already submerging, saltwater intrusion, President Tong purchased land in Fiji for relocation, 'climate refugees', Paris Agreement poster child); largest exclusive economic zone ratio (3.5 million km² ocean vs 811 km² land, 33 atolls + 1 raised coral island across 3 island groups spanning 3,500km); Battle of Tarawa (November 20-23, 1943, US Marines vs Japanese, 1,000+ US dead in 76 hours, one of bloodiest Pacific Theatre battles, Betio fortifications); Banaba (Ocean Island, phosphate mining 1900-79, British/Australian/NZ companies stripped island bare, Banabans forcibly relocated to Rabi Fiji, environmental devastation, colonial exploitation epitome); nuclear testing (Christmas Island/Kiritimati, British thermonuclear tests 1957-62, Operation Grapple, servicemen exposed, health effects); International Date Line (Kiribati moved dateline 1995 so all islands on same day, Line Islands UTC+14 first place to see new year); Phoenix Islands Protected Area (largest marine protected area when declared 2008, ~408k km², UNESCO); copra (dried coconut, primary export historically); te maneaba (community meeting house, traditional governance); seafaring (traditional navigation); fishing licenses (major revenue source, tuna); remittances (seafarers abroad on merchant ships); one of world's poorest countries; overcrowded South Tarawa (~60k on small atoll)

current_leader.name: Taneti Maamau
current_leader.title: President (Te Beretitenti)
current_leader.notes: Tobwaan Kiribati Party (TKP); re-elected 2020; shifted diplomatic recognition from Taiwan to China (2019, controversial, infrastructure deals); climate policy; South Tarawa development; less vocal on climate than predecessor Tong

former_leaders.name: Anote Tong
former_leaders.notes: BTK (Pillars of Truth); three terms; global climate champion ('our islands are drowning'); purchased Fiji land for potential relocation; Phoenix Islands Protected Area (world's largest marine reserve); Nobel Peace Prize nominee; raised Kiribati's profile internationally; 'migration with dignity' policy

former_leaders.name: Teburoro Tito
former_leaders.notes: MTM/National Progressive Party; recognised Taiwan; no-confidence vote 2003; nuclear testing compensation advocacy

former_leaders.name: Ieremia Tabai
former_leaders.notes: First president post-independence; independence architect; built state institutions; Banaba compensation negotiations; longest-serving founding leader
